Publications and displays, centralized payment of bills, publication of publicity literature in different languages about the achievements and development programs of the government, cultural programmes, publicity of achievements of the Government of Bihar within the state and through information and public relations created by the department. . Vision To disseminate and propagate government policies, programmes, schemes and achievements, effectively for public awareness. Documentation of progress and achievements of various department. To know and understand the mood, perception and feedback of people on different issues by analysis of news published in the media and to arrange quick response of governments views/ point among general public through media as necessary. To disseminate policies, programmes and achievements of various departments for educating people and mass communication by performing role of facilitator by using various, method and resources of educating people and mass communication. Formation of creativeness for publicity of programmes, schemes and achievements of various departments through poster, pamphlet, folder, booklet, etc. and to facilitate the advertisement work. The bill aims to improve efficiency, ensure independence, transpare...
national_raw_news.content: Lok Sabha has passed the Tribunals Reforms Bill, 2026. The Bill was passed without discussion amidst opposition uproar. As the pandemonium continued, the Chair adjourned the House for the day to meet again at 11:00 AM tomorrow. Earlier, when the House reassembled after the second adjournment at 2:00 PM, Minister of State for Law and Justice Arjun Ram Meghwal moved the Tribunals Reforms Bill, 2026, amid the opposition uproar. The bill aims to improve efficiency, ensure independence, transparency, and uniformity in the qualifications, appointment of service of Chairpersons and Members of various Tribunals, as well as the administration and functioning of the Tribunals. The legislation also proposes to establish a National Tribunals Commission. Mr Meghwal said that the Bill has been brought as part of the reform express being rolled out across various sectors under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. He said, the purpose of tribunals is not to replace courts but to function as complementary institutions in modern governance. They deal with specialized matters such as taxation, company law, environment, securities market, intellectual property, and other regulatory domains, with the objective of ensuring speedy and effective delivery of justice. Mr Meghwal highlighted that under the leadership of Mr Modi, the government initiated the process of rationalisation of tribunals in 2015. The Minister said that the Tribunal Reforms Bill, 2026 has been brought to establish a modern, independent, and uniform tribunal ecosystem. Mr Meghwal highlighted that the bill is aimed at strengthening governance, appointments, institutional independence, transparency, and efficiency. He said, the National Tribunals Commission will be established and it will be chaired by a former Judge of the Supreme Court or a former Chief Justice of a High Court. . The Presiding Officer, Jagdambika Pal repeatedly requested the protesting members to back to their seat and allow the House to function. He said that the entire nation is watching that who is responsible for the disruption of the House. Mr Pal said, the House is meant for discussion, but since the very first day of the Monsoon Session, the opposition members are continuously causing disruptions. Mr Pal said that Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju has already accepted their demand that Union Home Minister Amit Shah is ready to give a statement on the issue related to the student protest.

national_raw_news.title: 2 hours ago | National 31 Union Minister Kiren Rijiju appeals to opposition to allow HM Amit Shah to make statement
national_raw_news.content: Union Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju today said that the Government is ready for a detailed discussion in Parliament regarding the recent student protests and related issues. Assuring that Home Minister Amit Shah is ready to respond to every point, Mr Rijiju stated that citizens have a right to know the facts. He urged the Opposition to maintain order on the floor and refrain from further obstructing proceedings. Speaking to reporters at the Parliament premises after the Business Advisory Committee (BAC) meeting, Mr Rijiju appealed to the Opposition to allow the House to function so that Home Minister Amit Shah makes a statement about the students’ protest and addresses all concerns raised by the opposition members. The Minister emphasized that the Government has never shied away from parliamentary debates. He highlighted that during the BAC meeting, the government clearly communicated its willingness to hold a comprehensive discussion on the matter.

national_raw_news.title: 2 hours ago | National 85 India scripted successful conservation journey from 523 lions to 891 in last 10 years: PM Modi on...
national_raw_news.content: On the occasion of World Lion Day, Prime Minister Narendra Modi today said that India’s Asiatic lion population is thriving, with its habitat and range expanding. Sharing an article written by Union Minister Bhupender Yadav, Mr Modi highlighted that the Government’s unwavering commitment to conservation, backed by strong community participation, is an inspiring example of protecting the country’s wildlife and preserving the species for generations to come. The article written by Environment, Forest and Climate Change Minister Bhupendra Yadav points out that the lions’ range has expanded from around 30 thousand square kilometres in 2020 to nearly 35 thousand square kilometres, covering 11 districts. It also talks about how India scripted the successful conservation journey of 523 lions in 2015 to 891 in 2025.

national_raw_news.title: 3 hours ago | International 177 Over ten lakh people evacuated as typhoon Dolphin batters parts of Eastern China
national_raw_news.content: Chinese authorities have evacuated more than one million people from eastern China, including Shanghai, as Typhoon Dolphin made landfall. The typhoon brought heavy rain and disrupted transport across the region. Nearly 1,000 flights were cancelled in Shanghai today. Authorities have downgraded Dolphin to a tropical storm. China had earlier issued its highest-level red alert for Dolphin, which is the strongest storm to hit the country this year. Dolphin had maximum wind speeds of 150 kilometres per hour when it first struck Yuhuan in Zhejiang province yesterday. Heavy rain has been forecast for Shandong, Henan, Hubei, Anhui, Jiangsu and Zhejiang provinces. Shanghai is also expected to receive heavy rainfall. Authorities have urged people to avoid outdoor activities. Several major tourist attractions remain closed. These include parts of Disneyland and Legoland, as well as several viewing platforms along Shanghai’s Bund. State media footage showed ground-floor businesses flooded in Shanghai’s former French Concession. The area is popular with tourists. People were also seen wading through ankle-deep floodwaters.

national_raw_news.title: 7 hours ago | National 130 PM Modi urges citizens to participate enthusiastically in Har Ghar Tiranga movement
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has urged citizens to participate enthusiastically in the Har Ghar Tiranga movement and renew their collective resolve to contribute towards building a Viksit Bharat. In a social media post, Mr Modi said, ” Our Tricolour is our pride and a constant source of inspiration to always give our best for the nation.” The prime minister said he is glad that this year’s efforts are dedicated to Vande Mataram and that too at a time when we are marking its 150th anniversary. The Culture Ministry said the Har Ghar Tiranga campaign this year would seek to bring the spirit of patriotism to streets and homes across the country through Tiranga Yatras, Tiranga Rallies, Tiranga Concerts and mass singing of Vande Mataram. The ministry said the 150th anniversary of Vande Mataram would provide an opportunity for citizens to celebrate the national song as part of the Independence Day festivities. A key feature of this year’s celebrations will be ‘Suryapath Tiranga’, described by the ministry as a first-of-its-kind initiative aimed at bringing Indians across the world together in a global celebration of the Tricolour. The Ministry appealed to citizens to hoist the national flag at their homes and upload their selfies on the Har Ghar Tiranga website. The Har Ghar Tiranga campaign has emerged as a nationwide public participation initiative associated with Independence Day celebrations, encouraging citizens to display the national flag and express their connection with the country.

national_raw_news.title: Jharkhand students’ agitation over alleged irregularities in recruitment exams enters 17th Day
national_raw_news.content: The student agitation in Jharkhand over alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations entered its 17th day today. The students are marching towards the Vidhan Sabha, while elaborate security arrangements have been made by the police to prevent any untoward incident. Akashvani correspondent reports that led by the JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch, students are marching from Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium towards the Vidhan Sabha, demanding cancellation of the JSSC-CGL examination and a CBI probe into the alleged irregularities. The government claims that 98 per cent of the students’ demands have been accepted, but the protesters remain firm on their key demands. During the march, the students crossed the barricades near the Old Assembly and reached the seventh and final barricade, following which the police began using water cannons to stop them. Hunger-striking student leader Devendra Nath Mahto was brought to the Assembly in an ambulance, where he joined the march on a stretcher along with his supporters. Six students continue their indefinite hunger strike. Leader of Opposition Babulal Marandi, BJP state president Aditya Sahu, and several other BJP leaders and workers protesting outside Chief Minister Hemant Soren’s residence were detained. The agitation intensified further after the resignations of all three JPSC members were accepted. Meanwhile, the Enforcement Directorate has registered an ECIR in connection with the alleged JPSC examination irregularities. The students have said that their agitation will continue until their key demands, including cancellation of the JSSC-CGL examination and a CBI probe, are fulfilled.

national_raw_news.title: Former IRGC Chief Mohsen Rezaee appointed as Iran Supreme Leader’s representative to SNSC
national_raw_news.content: Iran’s Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei has appointed former Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) chief Mohsen Rezaee as his representative to the country’s Supreme National Security Council (SNSC), replacing Mohammad Baqir Zolghadr. The position was formerly held by Ali Larijani, who was assassinated in US-Israeli strikes in March, and then Mohammad Baqir Zolghadr. Rezaee is a former IRGC chief and a member of Iran’s Expediency Discernment Council, which resolves differences between parliament and the Guardian Council, a separate body that vets candidates for office. Rezaee was a military commander during the Iran-Iraq war of the 1980s, referred to in Iran as the ‘Sacred Defence’.
